chunks: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Wahhab narrated to us, he said: Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Yahya ibn al-Baqi narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Ghani narrated to us [he said]: Al-Mughani, he said: Abdul-Razzaq narrated to us, from Mandal, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas.
Regarding the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Peace be upon the Family of Yasin.'
Peace be upon the Family of Yasin.
He said: The peace is from the Lord of all the worlds upon Muhammad and his Family, may Allah bless him and them, and safety is for those who befriend them in the Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'Family of Yasin' mentioned in the Quran according to Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Ibn Abbas interprets 'the Family of Yasin' as Prophet Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt, linking the divine salutation to the concept of *tawalla* (allegiance). This interpretation underscores the Shia belief that the peace and safety promised on the Day of Resurrection are contingent upon recognizing and loving the Prophet’s pure progeny.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Abdullah bin Muhammed bin Abdul-Wahhab, that he said: We were told by Abu Muhammed, Abdullah bin Yahya bin Abdul-Baqi, that he said: We were told by my father, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Hasan bin Abdul-Ghani, that he said: Al-Mughani, that he said: We were told by Abdul-Razzaq, from Mandal, from Kalbi, from Abu Saleh, from Ibn Abbas,
with regards to the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Peace be upon the Family of Yasin.» [37:130]
[1] he said: The peace is from the Lord of all the worlds upon Muhammed and his Family, Allah’s blessings be upon him and upon, and peace is for those who befriend them in the Resurrection.
